chunk_findings.detail: The intent states that a rename "keeps body, globs, priority, tags **and notes**", but the re-filed record is built from an explicit field list — `title`, `parent`, `needs`, `globs`, `resources`, `body`, `tags`, `priority`, `line`, `kind`, `extra` (only `fixes`) — and no `notes` argument is passed. Nor is any event emitted afterwards that re-keys notes onto the new id: the only events appended in the locked step are `f"{d.family}.updated"` for dependents (needs only) and `item.abandoned` for `old`. Concretely: create/attach notes to item `X` (e.g. the note the operator would have carried by hand in the 2026-10-17 workflow this change replaces), then run `ddflow rename X Y`; `IT.add_task` produces `Y` without the notes, and the notes remain attached only to the abandoned tombstone `X` that no live view surfaces (`_dependents` explicitly ignores terminal/removed records, so nothing else in this file ever touches them). The result is exactly the silent feature loss the change claims to eliminate — `ddflow show Y` is missing content that `ddflow show X` had, and the command reports `item.renamed` success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rename.py:87 (`IT.TaskDraft(...)` in `rename`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated intent is that `rename` keeps "body, globs, priority, tags and notes", but the only test that verifies field preservation (`test_rename_to_another_phase_carries_everything`, lines 62-68) asserts exactly body, tags, priority, parent and needs — and `notes` is asserted nowhere in this file (nor in any other file in the manifest: the only other test touched is `test_coherence_coverage.py`, and the golden files cover help/schema output, not item payloads). So the input "item with notes, rename it" is never exercised: an implementation that constructs the new item from title/parent/body/globs/tags/priority and silently drops the notes record leaves every assertion in this suite green, and the old id's notes either stay on the tombstone (`items["A"]`) or vanish, with no test able to tell the difference. Given that `notes` is the one field enumerated in the intent that is deliberately skipped in the test named "carries_everything", the claimed guarantee is unverified by this change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rename_item.py:test_rename_to_another_phase_carries_everything

chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated intent is that a rename "keeps body, globs, priority, tags and notes", but the `TaskDraft` built for the new id carries only `title, parent, needs, globs, resources, body, tags, priority, line, kind` and `extra={"fixes": ...}` — there is no `notes` field and no notes in `extra`. Given an item that has notes attached (e.g. `ddflow note DX-dispatch-launch "…"` before the rename), `rename DX-dispatch-launch P-agent-parity.dispatch-launch` re-files the item under the new id via `IT.add_task`, and the note records stay keyed to the old id, which is then abandoned. The new id therefore renders with no notes while the tombstone holds them, so the operator loses the notes on the live item — directly contradicting the documented behavior ("keeps … notes") and the motivating scenario, where the body and notes were the whole point of not re-filing by hand. The omission of `resources`/`needs` from the intent list and of `notes` from the docstring shows the two lists were not reconciled; if notes are an item field (as the intent asserts), this line drops them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rename.py:80 (IT.TaskDraft construction in rename)

chunk_findings.detail: `why = reason or f"renamed to {new}"` followed by `"reason": f"renamed to {new}: {why}"` duplicates the text whenever no explicit reason is supplied. Calling `rename(repo, "A-old", "A-new")` with the default `reason=""` records the tombstone abandon as `reason="renamed to A-new: renamed to A-new"`. The tombstone reason is the human-facing record of where the id went (and, per the module docstring, the thing that "names the new one"), so every plain rename writes a garbled reason; if the alias lookup or a `--repoint-to` suggestion ever parses that string, the doubled text is what it has to cope with.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rename.py:97 (reason composition before "item.abandoned")

chunk_findings.detail: `repoint` validates that the target `to` is a live item but never rejects `to == old`, whereas the sibling `rename` explicitly refuses that case ("the new id is the old one"). Input `repoint(repo, "item", "item")` — reachable from `abandon item --repoint-to item` — passes the target check (`st.items["item"]` is live), builds `entries` with `_moved(d.needs, "item", "item", d.id)`, i.e. the dependents' needs unchanged, and returns a successful `item.repointed` after writing no-op update events. The dependents are left needing `item`, which the surrounding abandon is about to make terminal, so the command reports the dependents as repointed while they are in fact stranded — exactly the failure ("an abandon that only WARNED about stranded dependents") this feature exists to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rename.py:112 (repoint)
